requirements.evidence: All contract items are present: the migration has a unique (entity_id, email) and cascade (create_entity_invites_table.php:16-42), the email mutator normalizes on every write (EntityInvite.php:39-50), the pending scope and TTL_DAYS=7 are there, sendInvite validates, checks for an existing member or pending invite, catches the unique-violation race and rate-limits only after a successful insert (Members.php:112-182), and accept/decline are idempotent and authorized (PendingInvites.php:367-422). The modal header uses ui.members_details, the select has no empty option, removal uses a confirmation modal, and pt_BR strings are added. Gaps: the expired-invite error on key `invite` only renders inside `@if ($invites->isNotEmpty())` (pending-invites.blade.php:2-7), so a user with no other pending invites never sees it. The race is only partly handled: updateOrCreate (Members.php:147) can silently update a pending row that another manager just committed instead of reporting an error.

conventions.evidence: Good: authorization goes through a new EntityPolicy::manageMembers and an EntityInvitePolicy; properties use #[Validate] and the code calls validateOnly; the migration has a generator-style timestamp name and a reversible down(); the model uses an explicit #[Fillable]; a reusable anonymous <x-modal> Blade component was added; CHANGELOG, business-rules.md and database-schema.md are updated. Deviation: the new domain writes (invite creation in Members::sendInvite, membership creation in PendingInvites::accept, role change in saveRole, cancelInvite) live inline in Livewire components instead of in app/Actions/* classes, as the conventions require.

security.evidence: Every public action authorizes on the server (sendInvite/cancelInvite: manageMembers; openMember: update; saveRole: assignRole; confirmRemoval: delete; accept/decline: invitee policy). IDs are resolved through scoped relations (`$this->entity->invites()->findOrFail`, `memberships()->findOrFail`). selectedMembershipId and confirmingRemoval are #[Locked]. Output is escaped with {{ }}. Invites are rate-limited per manager and entity. Small gaps: the updateOrCreate race can overwrite another manager's pending invite (role/inviter), and the public closeMember() is unauthorized (harmless, it only clears UI state).

tests.evidence: The tests are extensive and meaningful. MembersInviteTest covers the happy path, owner-role tampering, invalid e-mail, existing member, pending vs expired vs accepted invites, the unique race, the quota not being consumed by invalid input, the 10/hour limit per manager, unauthorized send/cancel, a foreign-entity cancel and the single help is-danger element. MembersDetailsTest covers the locked-property tamper, foreign membership, the owner being immutable, the last manager and unauthorized open/save/confirm. PendingInvitesTest covers case-insensitive listing, idempotent accept, expired accept, a non-invitee 403 and the onboarding <hr> presence/absence. EntityInviteMailTest checks both locales. Removed MembersTest cases belong to the deleted addMember/assignRole features and are replaced, not weakened.

simplicity.evidence: Lean overall. The repeated manager count is extracted into managerCount() (Members.php:327), the role select is reused, and the modal shell is a single small Blade component. createOrFirst gives no-duplicate membership in one line. Minor extra machinery: isUniqueViolation() string-sniffs the exception message (Members.php:334-340), and the pending check plus updateOrCreate plus catch is somewhat layered.

readability.evidence: Methods are small with PHPDoc and explanatory comments (e.g. 'Replaces an expired or accepted invite for this address; otherwise inserts.'). Names are clear and the style matches the existing sibling component. Minor points: an inline @php block computes $locked in members.blade.php:1218-1220; dates are hard-coded as 'd/m/Y' even in the English locale; and `array_merge($this->validateOnly(...), $this->validateOnly(...))` is a bit awkward.

scope.evidence: Nearly everything serves the task. The adjacent edits are justified by the manager-only requirement: the Dashboard isManager fix and dashboard.blade.php cleanup, the navbar @can('manageMembers'), and invite cleanup on entity soft-delete (Settings.php:84). The extra public closeMember() is a small addition beyond the contract.

issues.explanation: Domain writes (create/replace invite, accept into membership, change role, cancel invite) live in Livewire components instead of dedicated app/Actions/* classes, which the conventions require for domain writes.
The `invite` error from accepting an expired invite only renders inside the non-empty-list branch, so a user whose only invite expired never sees the message.

updateOrCreate on (entity, email) reports an error only for concurrent inserts; if another manager's pending invite is committed between the pending check and the lookup, it is silently overwritten (role, inviter, expiry) instead of rejected.
Unique-violation detection relies on SQLSTATE 23000 plus message substrings, which is brittle across database drivers (Postgres uses 23505).
Dates are hard-coded to the 'd/m/Y' format regardless of locale.
closeMember() is an extra public endpoint not in the contract; harmless, but it widens the public surface.

review.summary: The change replaces direct member addition with an invite flow (table, model, factory, policy, queued markdown mail, PendingInvites component), makes the members page manager-only, and adds a details modal with explicit save and a removal confirmation modal. It is backed by thorough tests, including tamper and unauthorized cases, and by updated docs. It would be approved with nits; the main deviation is that domain writes are not extracted into Actions, plus small gaps around the expired-invite error display and the updateOrCreate race.
